# hands/lab

the lab ledger, Teeny's experiments on what gets attention.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/lab <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): propose [--source S]; conclude
- Job (writes state or calls the core): score [--id N]
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: list [--status open|concluded|all] [--limit N]; lessons [--max N]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `propose [--source S]` | A | `{surface: x\|moltbook, hypothesis, format, metric?, posts, deadline_days \| deadline: YYYY-MM-DD}`. |
| `score [--id N]` | J | For each open experiment (or one): its measured writes between the proposal and the deadline (`n`, `avg`) against the surface's other measured writes of the same kinds in the same period (`baseline_n`, `baseline_avg`), from the rows `hands/stats board` reads. |
| `conclude` | A | `{id, verdict: works\|fails\|unclear, lesson}`, the lesson one line of at most 200 characters. |
| `list [--status open\|concluded\|all] [--limit N]` | R | The experiments, newest first, open ones by default, each open one with its numbers as of now (computed, not stored) and `due`. |
| `lessons [--max N]` | R | The concluded experiments' lessons, newest first (10, at most 20), with verdict and numbers. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `conclude`, `lessons`, `list`, `propose`, `score`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--id`, `--limit`, `--max`, `--source`, `--status`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/lab <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
